# Coherent Time evolution

The Time evolution page uses a ground-hyperfine secular density matrix
$\rho=\rho_{F_a}\oplus\rho_{F_b}$, initially $I/N_g$. Every $m,m'$ element
within either manifold is retained. Inter-manifold coherences at the ground
hyperfine frequency are excluded. This is distinct from the ACC page's steady
population calculation and linear RF response.

For species $a$, in angular-frequency units,

$$
\dot\rho_a=-i[H_{B,a}/\hbar+u(t)H_{LS,a}/\hbar,\rho_a]
+u(t)\sum_j\mathcal D[J_{a,j}]\rho_a
+R_{ER,a}(\mathcal P[\rho_{I,a}\otimes I_2/2]-\rho_a)
+R_{u,a}(I\,\mathrm{Tr}\rho_a/N_a-\rho_a)
+R_{SE,a}(\mathcal P[\rho_{I,a}\otimes\rho_{S,a}]-\rho_a)
+R_{a\leftarrow b}(\mathcal P[\rho_{I,a}\otimes\rho_{S,b}]-\rho_a).
$$

Here $u(t)=1$ before pump turn-off and zero afterward,
$\mathcal D[J]\rho=J\rho J^\dagger-\{J^\dagger J,\rho\}/2$,
and $\mathcal P$ removes cross-hyperfine blocks. Nuclear and electron reductions
come from the coupled-to-uncoupled Clebsch–Gordan transformation. Electron
marginals are trace normalized; nuclear marginals retain the target trace.
Both species are evolved in a common lab-z basis, so electron spin transfer
does not depend on their independently selected display bases.

The static Hamiltonian is
$H_B/\hbar=2\pi(\mu_B/h)10^{-9}B_{\mathrm{nT}}\sum_F g_F P_F (\hat n_B\cdot\mathbf F) P_F$,
where $\hat n_B=(\sin\theta\cos\phi,\sin\theta\sin\phi,\cos\theta)$.
Both sidebar angles use integer degrees: $\theta$ is measured from +z and
$\phi$ from +x toward +y. The density matrix remains stored in lab-z.
The Hamiltonian uses dimensionless spin operators and the
existing signed hyperfine $g_F$, including the nuclear contribution. Thus
$\dot{\langle F_y\rangle}=-\omega_F\langle F_z\rangle$ for a field along x.
The linear Zeeman approximation is retained; Breit–Rabi mixing is excluded.

## Optical elimination and normalization

Each incoming ground manifold $F_i$ and excited manifold $F_e$ has a signed
absorption matrix $A_{ei}=\sum_q\epsilon_q d_q$, using the existing Wigner
dipoles and laboratory Jones polarization. If $r$ is the existing intensity
rate scale and $V$ its complex, peak-normalized Voigt response,

$$
J_{F_o,F_e,F_i,q}=\sqrt{r\,\mathrm{Re}V_{ei}}\,D_{F_o,F_e,q}A_{ei},\qquad
H_{LS}/\hbar=\tfrac12\sum_{ei}r\,\mathrm{Im}V_{ei}A_{ei}^\dagger A_{ei}.
$$

Emission matrices are normalized over all outgoing ground states and emitted
polarizations: $\sum_{F_o,q}D^\dagger D=I_e$. Each emission matrix retains the
amplitudes of all excited m states in that manifold. Splitting it into
independent m-resolved jumps would erase spontaneous coherence transfer and
break rotation covariance. Different incoming/outgoing hyperfine manifolds
and different excited F manifolds have separate jumps. Excited-hyperfine
interference and explicit excited-state precession are omitted.

On collinear diagonal states the dissipative populations reproduce the existing
optical rate generator. The dispersive Hamiltonian uses the same factor and
sign as the Light shift page. All active pumps, including off-target tails,
contribute to this dynamics. Pump-off removes both optical terms. Magnetic
shifts and light shifts are not fed back into optical detunings.

The use of an excited-state-eliminated ground master equation follows the
general approach discussed by [Chang, Guo and Qin, Phys. Rev. A 99, 063411
(2019)](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.99.063411). The specific Voigt weighting
and secular collective jumps above define this application's approximation.

## Bases, integration and detection

The sidebar has separate Open and Save controls beside Setting name. Build a
committed settings snapshot after rendering the sidebar. The shared Save helper
renders a browser-only button through `st.html`; it registers no Streamlit widget
event. On click, JavaScript reads only the live filename, updates the name in the
downloaded JSON and starts a Blob download. Pointer/mouse-down prevents input
blur, so unfinished physical inputs are not committed. There is no app or
fragment rerun. ACC's inactive-pump fragment refreshes its snapshot separately
when committed controls change. Loading retains current-format validation and
the page-isolated callback.
After each load attempt, a session-only revision gives the uploader a fresh
identity, retaining Open as a button instead of an uploaded-file chip and
allowing the same file to be selected again. This revision is not saved.

The page offers section CSV downloads. The complete export helper described
below remains available programmatically; its former bottom-page button is removed.

All result expanders use native `on_change="rerun"` tracking with independent
per-species keys. Zeeman populations, Atomic moments and Steady-state probe signal scanning
default to closed. Content is guarded by the container's `.open` state: chart creation,
section CSV preparation and widgets run only while open. Steady-state convergence
and spectral readout are inside the scan guard, so they do not run on initial
page load. Transient integration is also inside the combined guard for the three
time-domain sections. All closed means no transient solve, even after physical
edits; scan-only rendering computes only the stationary state. One trajectory
retrieval per rerun is shared by both species. Persistent setting keys
preserve axes, moment/probe choices and scan limits across hidden-widget cleanup;
expander visibility is session UI state outside the saved-condition format.

Auto update and Apply are native widgets inside a horizontal `st.bottom`
container, pinned below the scrolling main content. Shared screen-only CSS in
the entry point halves the native bottom padding from 3.5rem to 1.75rem. The
row does not wrap. Auto update defaults on. In manual mode, fingerprints of the applied physical
inputs and transient timing gate the calculations. Pending physical edits hide
the affected curves and downloads until Apply; a timing edit gates transients
only. Applying with all sections closed records the fingerprints without a
solve. Probe readout and display settings are excluded from these fingerprints.
Auto update is a persistent page-session preference, not a saved condition field.

`ui/time_evolution_cache.py` separates two transient entries below 8 MiB from
one entry at or above that estimated density size. The estimate uses the same
Larmor-driven sample rule and full complex density dimensions as the solver.
Four display entries retain only populations, moments and metadata, removing
the rotated density trajectory before caching. Steady-state and probe-readout
caches retain four entries each; spectra retain eight. These are entry limits,
not a process-wide memory cap: live results, serialization and temporary
rotations still consume memory. Evicted physical inputs are recomputed.
The separate solver version invalidates transient and stationary cache entries
when the numerical policy changes without changing the physical-model identity.

Each species has independent display axes for populations and moments. The
physical integration and probe remain in laboratory z. The Zeeman axis defines
the displayed populations and exported coherences; the moment axis defines
electron polarization and local alignment. Changing either only re-expresses
the cached density matrix, without repeating integration. Both are independent
of the field direction. The local
transverse frames remain cyclic: q=z uses (x,y,z), q=x uses (y,z,x), and q=y
uses (z,x,y). The output is $U_q^\dagger\rho_{lab}U_q$, with the corresponding
spin rotation. Hyperfine totals, laboratory orientation and probe signals are
invariant under this change of basis. Complete CSVs record both axes; population
and coherence columns use the Zeeman frame while moment columns use the moment
frame. Section CSV metadata identifies the relevant frame and both selections.

The moment readout contracts the complete output density matrix with operators
in that same basis. Laboratory orientation uses
$U_q^\dagger F_j U_q/\hbar$, $j=x,y,z$, and is independent of the chosen basis.
In local coordinates $(u,v,q)$, the transverse alignment operators are
$Q_{uv}=(F_uF_v+F_vF_u)/2$ and $Q_{uu}-Q_{vv}=F_u^2-F_v^2$.
Their expectation values are divided by $\hbar^2$ and retain coherences.
All manifold-resolved moments are per total atom, without division by manifold
population. CSVs identify u and v explicitly; the complete export includes
all calculated moments even when their graphs are hidden.

The displayed hyperfine polarization is the scalar
$\langle\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf I\rangle/\hbar^2$. Since $\mathbf F=\mathbf I+\mathbf S$
and $S=1/2$, its eigenvalue in a ground-F manifold is
$[F(F+1)-I(I+1)-3/4]/2$. Thus the full-ensemble expectation is
$(I/2)P(F_a)-[(I+1)/2]P(F_b)$. Within-F coherences do not contribute to this
scalar operator, which is proportional to the identity within each block.
It vanishes for $I/N_g$, lies between $-(I+1)/2$ and $I/2$, and is independent
of quantization axis. The complete CSV exports it as the dimensionless
`hyperfine_polarization` field, alongside the retained manifold totals.

Complex adaptive integration runs separately on each side of the switch,
with relative tolerance $2\times10^{-10}$ and absolute tolerance $10^{-12}$.
`DensityDynamics` prepares state boundaries, constant dark/pump generators,
electron-randomization maps and uniform-relaxation maps once per solve. Only
the evolving nuclear/electron marginals and nonlinear spin-exchange targets
are evaluated in the derivative. For $T=R(n\otimes\bar e)$,
$\bar e=e/\mathrm{Tr}(e)$, the exact differential is
$dT=R(dn\otimes\bar e+n\otimes d\bar e)$ with
$d\bar e=(de-\bar e\,d\mathrm{Tr}(e))/\mathrm{Tr}(e)$.
BDF receives the resulting analytic complex Jacobian, including cross-species
off-diagonal blocks. The normalization derivative is retained for off-trace
trial states. The stationary probe solver uses the same prepared derivative
and Jacobian while retaining its convergence criteria and accuracy refinements.
The method is selected by a conservative rate heuristic. For each species,
the coherent scale is the infinity norm of the magnetic commutator plus the
pump AC-Stark commutator when pumps are on. The damping scale is
$R_u+2(R_{\mathrm{ER}}+R_{\mathrm{SE,self}}+R_{\mathrm{SE,cross}})$ plus the
infinity norm of the optical generator after subtracting its AC-Stark
commutator. The factor two is a conservative estimate for the two marginals
in spin-exchange targets; this is a performance heuristic rather than a
spectral stiffness proof. Taking the maximum of each scale over all active
species, DOP853 is selected only when the coherent scale times interval
duration is at least $2\pi$ and damping does not exceed the coherent scale.
Otherwise BDF remains selected. A failed or nonfinite DOP853 result retries
the complete interval with BDF from the original state, with identical
output times and tolerances. Persistent integration failures remain errors.
The transient cache includes an independent solver-policy version, so a
solver-policy update invalidates old trajectories without changing the
physical-model identifier or settings schema. Stationary probe scans retain
their existing BDF convergence procedure.
The result checks trace, Hermiticity and eigenvalue positivity before correcting
only numerical roundoff. Samples are allocated approximately in proportion to
interval duration, include the switch once, and target 20 samples per cycle
through the fastest possible rank-$2F$ Larmor harmonic. At 20,001 output samples
the page explicitly warns of possible undersampling. This cap does not change
the adaptive internal integration steps. Very fast precession over long
intervals can require substantial computation.

The detector contracts the complete density matrix with the existing Mathur
tensor, $\langle\alpha_{ab}\rangle=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\alpha_{ab})$, then propagates
the Jones vector through the uniform cell. The probe contributes no Hamiltonian
or relaxation. The complete CSV includes real and imaginary parts of every
independent upper-triangular within-F coherence; populations provide the
diagonal and Hermiticity supplies the lower triangle. They use the selected
Zeeman display basis and are dimensionless probabilities per total atom.

## Pump-on steady-state probe scan

`physics/probe_scan.py` builds the same coupled coherent master equation in
laboratory z and starts from the same unpolarized state. Pumps remain on for
the entire convergence calculation. Autonomous BDF intervals grow until two
consecutive intervals have a maximum state change below $10^{-9}$ and a small
stationary residual. For each species the residual tolerance is $10^{-10}$
times its smallest positive dissipative rate plus a floating-point allowance
of $100\epsilon$ times its fastest generator scale. The initial interval is
the inverse of the smallest positive dissipative rate. Integration starts at
`rtol=2e-10`, `atol=1e-12`; 30 intervals are allowed. Intervals double while
the maximum state change exceeds $10^{-9}$. Once changes are small, intervals
stop growing. If any species still fails its residual threshold and its
residual has not fallen by more than a factor of two over the last interval,
both integration tolerances tighten by a factor of 100 (with a relative
tolerance floor of $2.5\times10^{-14}$). The solver continues from the current
state over the original interval length. This removes small numerical
coherences whose derivative can exceed the stationarity threshold, without
relaxing that threshold or changing the physical equation. At most three
accuracy refinements are allowed; another stall reports an error. Cases that
converge normally retain the original accuracy. These refinements apply only
to the probe-scan stationary solver. A stationary initial state is
returned directly. Trace, Hermiticity and positivity are checked before readout.
Failure to converge is reported rather than labeling a transient state steady.
This convergence time is independent of the user event-sequence times.

`density_probe_spectrum` evaluates the existing all-hyperfine-channel complex
polarizability sweep. Its frequency coordinate is relative to the bare
fine-structure D-line center; pressure shifts remain in the transition centers.
For a fixed density matrix, the unit-coefficient scalar, vector and rank-2
operators are contracted once. Their frequency-dependent coefficients are
then combined into the transverse $2\times2$ polarizability at each detuning.
Time and frequency readout share exact Jones propagation and Stokes conversion.
The continuous weak probe does not enter the stationary master equation.

Each species scans 2001 equally spaced points over its saved bounds. Defaults
are ±7000 MHz; a native two-handle range slider allows ±10000 MHz with a
minimum 10 MHz span, enforced when the handles meet. It writes the existing
independent minimum/maximum settings without changing the saved format. Changing
the limits reuses the cached steady state. Probe line, direction, polarization
and path length are inherited; its fixed detuning/reference transition and the
display quantization axes do not constrain the frequency scan. CSVs contain
plotted signals and frequency-origin, probe/cell/pump and convergence metadata.

The scan section uses native 30%/70% columns. On the left, the shared ACC
population renderer shows the converged pump-on populations in the selected
Zeeman display basis, with aligned numerical m positions and a common y scale
for both manifolds. The responsive population chart has a combined 338-pixel
height, 30% taller than one signal chart. ACC retains its existing
Matplotlib renderer; the fixed-height scan uses native Vega-Lite bars from the
same aligned population data. On the right are the signal plots.
Each scan population bar spans 1/1.3 magnetic-quantum-number units, giving gaps
30% of the bar width, versus ACC's unchanged 0.72-unit bars;
both renderers put F on the vertical axis and omit gridlines. Two native
169-pixel chart viewports with no intervening gap give 338 pixels in total.
Both reserve identical horizontal-axis space; the upper axis labels and title
are transparent so the two plotting areas have equal heights. The upper
panel has a -20-pixel bottom margin to halve the visible gap; this overlap
uses only hidden axis space and reduces the stack footprint by 20 pixels.
The CSV repeats these steady populations as `population_F*_m*` columns and
identifies their quantization axis, alongside both field angles in degrees.

The scan header uses native containers for three signal checkboxes in one horizontal row, a range slider
and right-aligned section controls. Every section places help and download at
the right end of its top control row. Time-domain plots use two equal columns.
The slider's visible label stays on one line on its left; its 338-pixel container is twice as long
as the previous 169-pixel layout. Controls wrap when space is limited. The help button retains its full 56-pixel width.
Each species has an independent
`plotted_scan_signals_A/B` list. Its default order is Optical rotation then
Absorption; Ellipticity starts unchecked. Toggled plots append in check order.
The CSV includes selected signal columns and all steady population bars.
An empty signal selection still displays populations and permits their download.

All four result sections use native open-state gating: closed sections build
no charts, section controls or exports on sidebar reruns. Zeeman populations,
Atomic moments and Steady-state probe signal scanning default closed; Probe signal defaults
open. Saved atomic-moment defaults select hyperfine polarization and F_z.
All eight section-state keys (four per species) use the existing persistent
page-setting registry so Streamlit's hidden-widget cleanup does not reset them
when navigating away. Open/closed states remain session UI preferences.
Independent `plotted_probe_signals_A/B` lists select time-domain probe curves
and exported columns, defaulting to Absorption and Optical rotation. The
frequency scan has its own independent selections and defaults.

Settings format 2.8 and the v3 coherent model identifier are both required.
Earlier settings are rejected without migration, as requested by the user.

The **Zeeman populations** title row in **Steady-state probe signal scanning**
includes a density-matrix CSV download. It contains every matrix element,
including zero entries and both real and imaginary parts. Row and column
indices, F,m labels and the axis unit vector identify the selected scan basis; probabilities are
normalized per total atom. The matrix follows the scan population axis and records its Euler-basis convention. The download reuses the converged steady state.

Small ticks beneath the probe-scan detuning slider track mark all allowed
hyperfine transition centers within its full +/-10000 MHz domain. They include
the current pressure shift and use the same centers as the signal plots.

## Section fragments

Each A/B result section creates its expander inside its own `st.fragment`.
Opening or collapsing it therefore reruns that fragment, including its open
state gate, without rebuilding the sidebar or unrelated plots. A closed section
returns before reading calculation caches or preparing charts and exports.
Transient sections share one lazily retrieved trajectory for the current page
conditions; a physical sidebar change starts a new page render and invalidates
that local reference. The bounded calculation caches continue to match inputs.
Manual Apply gates are also checked inside every section fragment.

Fragment reruns preserve registered settings before any widgets can disappear,
so closing a section retains its axis choices. They refresh the existing
browser-only Save snapshot using the same helper as ACC pump fragments.
Shared moment selections request a full display refresh
because they affect other views; opening and collapsing never request one.
Native fragment-request regression tests retain the runner's fragment storage
and message queue, checking actual partial reruns rather than simulated full
page reruns. They cover both species, cache reuse, navigation, Save and Apply.

## Independent scan population basis

The scan selector precedes its signal checkboxes and has independent A/B
settings `probe_scan_axis_A/B`, default z. Choices are x, y, z, B direction,
probe major and probe minor. The transient Zeeman axis never enters this view.
B direction follows the signed physical field. At zero field, the configured
spherical direction remains the reference. For local transverse unit vectors
$a,b$ and input azimuth $\psi$, probe major is
$\cos\psi\,a+\sin\psi\,b$ and probe minor is
$-\sin\psi\,a+\cos\psi\,b$. Their cross product is the probe propagation
direction. These input axes are independent of helicity; circular polarization
uses the azimuth reference axes because no unique major/minor geometry exists.

Only the stationary display matrix is rotated. For direction $(\theta,\phi)$,
$U=\exp(-i\phi F_z)\exp(-i\theta F_y)$ and
$\rho_q=U^\dagger\rho_{\rm lab}U$, using dimensionless spin matrices.
The Euler convention fixes otherwise arbitrary coherence phases. Population
and full-matrix CSVs record the selected axis, its laboratory unit vector,
Euler angles and basis convention. The internal state and Jones spectra remain
in lab-z. The four-entry display cache holds only small stationary matrices.
Saved condition format 2.8 requires both new fields; older files are rejected
under the current-format-only policy.
